prompt: A B2B SaaS company (ARR ~$40M, currently flat-rate per-seat pricing) is considering shifting new contracts to usage-based pricing. Write the business case for the executive team, including the biggest financial risk.
context: Current pricing: $120/seat/month flat, average 45 seats/account, ~180 enterprise accounts. Product usage data (internal analytics) shows the top 20% of accounts by usage consume roughly 3x the platform resources of the median account but pay the same per-seat price. Competitor benchmarking (2 named competitors, publicly disclosed pricing pages) shows both have moved to usage-based or hybrid pricing in the last 18 months. Finance estimates that a naive switch to pure usage-based pricing could make revenue less predictable quarter-to-quarter, since usage-based SaaS companies in public filings have historically shown 10-20% higher revenue variance than seat-based peers.

binaryCriteria.description: Uses the fact that top-20%-usage accounts consume ~3x resources at flat pricing to justify why usage-based (or hybrid) pricing better matches value to cost.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the recommendation only cites competitor moves without referencing the internal usage-skew data.

binaryCriteria.description: Explicitly identifies revenue predictability/variance as the primary financial risk of a full usage-based switch, referencing the variance benchmark given.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Pass if the 10-20% variance figure (or an equivalent framing of predictability risk) appears as a named risk, not just an afterthought.

binaryCriteria.description: Recommends a specific mitigation approach (hybrid pricing, grandfathering, or phased rollout to new logos) rather than an all-or-nothing switch.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer only says "monitor closely" with no structural mitigation.

goldNotes: A strong answer recommends a hybrid model (base seat fee + usage overage) rather than a binary switch, explicitly reasoning from the fact that the top 20% of accounts consume ~3x resources but pay flat pricing (i.e., the current model under-monetizes heavy users and doesn't reflect value delivered). It should flag revenue predictability/variance as the central financial risk, citing the 10-20% variance benchmark, and recommend a mitigation (e.g., grandfathering existing contracts, phasing usage pricing to new logos first) rather than an abrupt company-wide switch. A weak answer treats this as "switch pricing to look competitive" without grounding the recommendation in the usage-skew data.
